test_title: PYST 5 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 13 Nov, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

Necessity being the mother of invention, he resourcefully modifies the Rover to go on long drives even though __**it have originally designed for short one.**__

options.text: it has originally have been designed for short one
it has originally been designed for short ones
it has originally was designed for short ones
it has originally has been designed to short one

solution:
The correct answer is '2', i.e. 'it has originally been designed for short ones'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence mentions that the Rover was designed for short drives but was modified for long drives, which describes an action that was completed in the past (designing the Rover).
 
• The use of **“has been”** in the correct option highlights the past action of designing the Rover while maintaining relevance to the present context.
 
• The word **“ones”** is used to correctly replace the plural noun "short drives."

Correct sentence: *Necessity being the mother of invention, he resourcefully modifies the Rover to go on long drives even though it has originally been designed for short ones*.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: **"it has originally have been designed for short one" – Incorrect because of the unnecessary use of “have” and the singular form “one” instead of “ones.”
 
• **Option 3: **"it has originally was designed for short ones" – Incorrect because "has" and "was" cannot be used together; they create a grammatical error.
 
• **Option 4: **"it has originally has been designed to short one" – Incorrect because of redundancy in "has" and "has been" and the use of the singular form “one” instead of “ones.”
